builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: DUET: Dual-Sparse Inference for Block Diffusion Language Models
summary: Duet replaces full-prefix attention and full-block propagation at every denoising step in block diffusion language models with a reused compact historical KV subset and query pruning that sends only likely-updated positions through the suffix Transformer layers, all without retraining. It costs implementation complexity in KV selection and shallow-layer update prediction, plus a modest accuracy risk that the paper reports as small but nonzero. It can fail if attention concentration or cross-step stability does not hold on the reader's prompts, if the underlying model is an autoregressive rather than a block-diffusion LM, or if predicted update positions miss tokens that actually needed deep computation.
rationale: The speedups are meaningful for a 24 GB or API-constrained setup, but the technique only applies if the reader runs block diffusion models such as LLaDA or SDAR, so workload-specific validation on their model and prompts is required before production adoption.
technique: Dual-sparse inference for block diffusion language models

claims.statement: Duet replaces full-prefix attention and full-block propagation at every denoising step in block diffusion language models with a reused compact historical KV subset and query pruning that sends only likely-updated positions through the suffix Transformer layers, all without retraining. It costs implementation complexity in KV selection and shallow-layer update prediction, plus a modest accuracy risk that the paper reports as small but nonzero. It can fail if attention concentration or cross-step stability does not hold on the reader's prompts, if the underlying model is an autoregressive rather than a block-diffusion LM, or if predicted update positions miss tokens that actually needed deep computation.
Maintains competitive accuracy with 1.34x/2.83x end-to-end/per-step speedups on LLaDA2.1-mini and 2.41x/4.72x on SDAR-8B-Chat-b32 at 32K context length.
